+# Geographic feasibility contract
+
+T24 keeps the approved game constraints intact while measuring the existing implementation.
+The [first-iteration numerical contract](contract-proposal.md) was approved by the owner:
+40×40 CSS px hit areas, 44 px maximum-coordinate label separation, and an 800×460 board
+inside an 800×540 window. Coordinate, area and coast-centre tolerances are named in
+[parameters.mjs](parameters.mjs). The >=99% / <=50-candidate target is an objective to
+measure, not an assumption that the current generator achieves it.
+
+The approved rules are pinned in the proposal. In particular the canonical island-graph
+degree cap is **four**, even though production currently permits five. Country degree
+remains 2–5; crossings remain 14–18. No production files change here.
+
+## Run the acceptance
+
+Use Node 24 (22.15+ provides the TypeScript loader hooks, but this task was measured on 24):
+
+```sh
+node docs/prototypes/new-game/T24/probe.mjs
+node --test docs/prototypes/new-game/T24/contract.test.mjs
+node docs/prototypes/new-game/T24/mutations.mjs
+git diff --check
+```
+
+The task's 15 individual `--test-name-pattern` commands work as written. Tests began as
+parent-authored positive/mutated controls, committed before the checker. The retained
+mock transcripts show that a fixture mock passes while an accept-everything fake fails
+all negative cases. The real checker is then independently deletion-mutated one group
+at a time; each group must fail through assertions, then the saved bytes are restored
+in a `finally` and the complete suite reruns. Evidence records identical restoration hashes.
+
+Each probe/mutation run creates a fresh tracked-path evidence directory and prints its
+location. Earlier measurements are never overwritten. Default runs use all seeds 0–99
+and stop at the first accepted candidate or after 50 attempts. Per-seed files retain every
+candidate's map/scene hash, failure groups, observed attempt number and time, with detailed
+first-attempt failures. A continuous existing game RNG stream is used, advancing once
+after each rejected body just as the production retry boundary does. A source snapshot
+and a reproducibility hash distinguish semantic results from machine-dependent timings.
+
+`targetMet: false` is a valid measurement outcome; the CLI still exits zero if the
+measurement and its positive control ran correctly. It never silently reports a failed
+rate as success. A broken witness or runtime failure exits nonzero. Read the report's
+`targetMet`, not just the process exit status, before authorising downstream work.
+
+## What the checks establish
+
+[contract.mjs](contract.mjs) audits graph invariants and all five fairness checks.
+[geometry.mjs](geometry.mjs) checks finite simple polygons, containment/overlap, actual
+shared boundary lengths (including split/T-junction edges), exposed coasts, and route
+intersections. Point contacts are not borders. Coast chains comprise exposed directed
+edge pieces facing the destination island centre; contiguous pieces form chains. Choose
+the longest chain, with lexicographic start-point tie-break, then its arc-length midpoint.
+Every route endpoint must be on that country's exposed coast and within 1 CSS px of it.
+The route interior cannot touch or pass through land, including its source/destination.
+Sea routes may cross other sea routes: this probe does not certify visual lane separation.
+
+Label checks scale positions into the agreed compact board, require 40 px hit squares
+inside their countries and frame, and check 44 px maximum-coordinate spacing. The maximum
+coordinate distance avoids the mistake of using Euclidean separation alone for square
+hit areas. The 14 px text / 4.5:1 contrast fields express the schematic's specification;
+they are not measurements of a running browser. T52 must measure actual rendered text,
+palette, hit targets and ownership cues. No metadata can substitute for that UI acceptance.
+
+The [witness](witness.mjs) is a hand-arranged rectangular subdivision with 46 countries,
+nine islands and 16 crossings. Its geometry, ports and water paths are built independently
+of the checker, and it is inspected by the same checks as the baseline. This is **one
+schematic compatibility example**, not a new production generator, 100 different maps,
+visual approval, or a demonstrated generation success rate. Its SVG is a technical drawing.
+
+[existing.mjs](existing.mjs) reads production TypeScript without modifying it, applies the
+existing layout and coast function, and retains exact graph/polygon/label information.
+Its sea path diagnostics sample production's quadratic formula at 16 intervals; positive
+curved-path clearance is not certified. The centre endpoints are exact and already fail
+the coast requirement. Hit-size bounding-box estimates are upper bounds, and unmeasured
+contrast is marked unknown, never invented. The substantive border/gap/spacing failures
+do not depend on those unknown metadata fields or curve approximation.
+
+## Next gate
+
+The report must distinguish joint compatibility (a witness) from generator performance
+(the seed sweep). An existing implementation failing every trial does not prove the
+constraint set mathematically impossible. Preserve failures and the owner's constraints;
+obtain owner review of the resulting evidence before downstream algorithm work. The
+reference-board task also requires approval of exact topology and appearance. Do not
+promote this schematic as the intended Isle-Pro-like visual direction.
+
+## Measured result
+
+The authoritative [full-source-fingerprinted sweep](evidence/runs/run-bbMp5F/report.json)
+found **0/100 successful seeds after 5,000 candidates** (50 per seed). The witness passed
+all 15 groups. Every candidate failed cells, borders, coasts, intersections and labels;
+157 also failed remoteness/island degree. All other graph/fairness groups passed.
+
+The [schematic SVG](evidence/runs/run-bbMp5F/witness.svg) and
+[complete witness data](evidence/runs/run-bbMp5F/witness.json) show the positive control.
+[All acceptance pattern outputs](evidence/acceptance-v1/summary.json) pass, and
+[all 15 guard-deletion mutants](evidence/mutations/run-qjxt9M/report.json) were killed
+with byte-identical restoration and all 85 tests passing afterward.
+
+The earlier run-NKe9GQ sweep is retained as a preliminary measurement under the original
+checker (commit 9fd8f2f); it predates the explicit tiny-slit and finite-text regressions
+and full prototype-source fingerprinting. The authoritative rerun above includes those
+fixes. Both report zero existing-implementation successes; neither is proof that no
+future geographic generator can meet the target. The source-fingerprinted report is
+the result to use for decisions.
+
+The existing layout therefore needs geographic construction rather than more retries.
+Carry the current graph/fairness checks forward, but derive land links from actual
+shared subdivisions and choose sea endpoints from exposed coastline midpoints. Begin
+with an owner-approved reference board (T25) after owner review of this feasibility
+evidence. Keep the 99% / 50-attempt generation objective unproven until T34–T36 measure
+the replacement; this task does not authorise silent relaxation or production changes.
+
+## Review R1: protect scaled separation independently
+
+Kimi's round-1 review proved that deleting `*scale` from the spacing check left
+all 85 tests passing: the old resize control failed through hit-square containment
+instead of spacing. [The reproduced pre-fix result](evidence/rework-r1/before-tests.txt)
+is retained. The added control uses an enlarged frame giving scale 0.8: 50-unit
+cells still contain 40px hit squares exactly, but labels are only 40px apart, so
+only the 44px spacing check rejects them. It additionally asserts that every
+reported error is a spacing error, preventing the former confounding refusal.
+
+The [updated mutation audit](evidence/mutations/run-Po8FYb/report.json) kills all
+16 mutants: the 15 complete-group deletions and the targeted scale-only deletion.
+Source bytes restore exactly; all 86 tests then pass. The
+[updated task-pattern outputs](evidence/rework-r1/acceptance-v2/summary.json) also
+pass. The original 82/85-test and 15-mutant evidence remains historical evidence,
+not a claim about the extended suite. No production, checker or probe behaviour
+changed for R1, and every authoritative sweep source fingerprint still matches.
+Unknown contrast remains explicit; only a rendered UI check in T52 can establish it.

+# Geography contract for the feasibility probe
+
+The owner accepted these numerical values for the first iteration in the session
+following PR #105 (2026-10-15). The original proposal wording below is retained
+as design provenance. Acceptance does not establish the generation target.
+
+Sources: [canonical board rules](https://github.com/diegoami/isle-wars-archaeology/blob/ae298e37c2f5177039e55767607f9345b6cb0e7a/design/core-rules.md#the-board),
+[UI legibility](https://github.com/diegoami/isle-wars-archaeology/blob/ae298e37c2f5177039e55767607f9345b6cb0e7a/design/ui.md#legibility-and-size),
+and the owner's coast-centred crossing requirement. This is a proposed numerical
+contract for T24's probe, not permission to change a rule or a claim of generation success.
+
+## Constraints already decided
+
+| Check | Requirement |
+| --- | --- |
+| Counts | Exactly 46 distinct countries; nine distinct islands, sizes 3,3,3,3,5,5,7,7,10; each country in exactly one island, consistent with its island field |
+| Symmetry | Every land/sea edge exists in both directions; no missing endpoint, self edge, duplicate edge or wrong land/sea island classification |
+| Connectivity | The whole country graph, each island's land graph and the island graph are connected |
+| Degree | Every country has 2–5 distinct neighbours, including crossings |
+| Cells | Every country is a finite, positive-area, connected simple polygon; island silhouette is exactly its subdivision; interiors do not overlap; no unexplained gaps or overlaps between islands |
+| Borders | Land edges are exactly the within-island pairs sharing a positive-length boundary; a point contact does not create an edge |
+| Crossings | 14–18 undirected sea edges between islands; exactly one rendered route per edge |
+| Coasts | Route endpoints belong to the intended countries and lie at the arc-length midpoint of a maximal exposed coast chain facing the destination island; ties deterministic |
+| Intersections | The route interior avoids all country interiors, including re-entry into its own endpoint countries; routes may meet their intended coast only at their ends |
+| Bonus | Each island pays max(2, floor(size/2) + distinct entrance countries), never above size |
+| Fortress | No island of >=7 countries has one entrance; at most three islands have one entrance |
+| Concentration | Single-entrance island bonuses sum to at most one quarter of all bonuses |
+| Remoteness | Every island is at most four crossings from every other, and touches at most four other islands |
+| Crowding | No country carries more than two crossings |
+| Labels | Fit the approved minimum window with non-overlapping legible owner/count badges and hit areas; generator positions provide spacing |
+
+The pinned design's island-neighbour maximum is four. Production currently exports
+five in board-gen.ts/board-fairness.ts. This probe uses four, irrespective of that
+implementation difference. The parent smoke found no violations of four on seeds 0–99;
+this sample does not prove that production's looser guard cannot admit one elsewhere.
+
+## Numerical proposals for owner decision
+
+These are **[designed]** values: the canonical sources above and T23 inventory were
+searched; they fix the window but leave spacing/tolerances and generation budget open.
+
+| Property | Recommended value and meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| Minimum viewport | 800×540 CSS px, already approved in UI13 |
+| Probe's compact panel allowance | 80 CSS px total height, leaving an 800×460 board; an explicit allocation, not a measured final UI |
+| Country hit area | At least 40×40 CSS px; the approved design proposes 40 |
+| Label separation | At least 44 CSS px in the maximum-coordinate distance: 40 px badge/hit square plus 4 px gutter. This also guarantees at least 44 px Euclidean separation |
+| Count text | At least 14 CSS px, with >=4.5:1 contrast; both are the canonical UI proposals. Geometry alone cannot prove font/contrast rendering; T52 must measure the scene |
+| Reference frame | 800×460 for probe fixtures. Other frames scale to the same board area with aspect preserved; spacing is checked after scaling, never in unscaled source units |
+| Coordinate tolerance | 0.000001 reference unit for collinearity/point-on-edge comparisons; never a visual gap allowance |
+| Area tolerance | 0.0001 square reference units for accumulated subdivision-area arithmetic; explicit gap/overlap geometry is still checked |
+| Coast-centre tolerance | At most 1 CSS px from the computed chain midpoint; endpoints must still lie on the correct exposed coast |
+| Candidate generation budget | Target >=99% valid boards within at most 50 candidate attempts per seed, with explicit failure on exhaustion. This is a proposed downstream target, not a measured result or permission to retry a deterministic bad layout |
+
+The alternative spacing is 40 CSS px with no extra gutter. Keep 44 unless measurements
+show it prevents feasible subdivision; do not quietly shrink either the hit area or window.
+
+## What the first measurement establishes
+
+Run from this task's worktree with Node 24:
+
+```sh
+node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning docs/prototypes/new-game/T24/evidence/preflight/smoke.mjs
+```
+
+[baseline-v1.json](evidence/preflight/baseline-v1.json) retains every seed 0–99,
+one observed existing generator-body attempt per seed, map/scene hashes and timings.
+All 100 bodies returned boards. Minimum rendered label separation at the assumed
+800×460 board is 29.588 CSS px (Euclidean) / 28.884 CSS px (maximum-coordinate distance),
+below either spacing proposal. This is a failing baseline for label packing, not a proof
+that the proposed constraint set is impossible. It has not run the full geometry contract.
+
+T24 will distinguish a static jointly valid schematic witness, if one is found, from
+the seed sweep of the existing implementation. A witness proves compatibility of the
+constraints; it does not prove a generator meets its success rate, visual quality or variety.
+No synthetic fixture or relabelled copy may be reported as 100 distinct generated boards.
+The full probe must retain per-constraint failures and attempt counts, including failures;
+reruns write fresh evidence rather than overwrite measured outputs.
+
+Numerical contract approval is required by T24's label acceptance line and Hazards.
+Downstream algorithm work additionally requires the resulting feasibility evidence and
+owner approval; a failed existing baseline alone is no proof of joint infeasibility.

+    ['duplicate rendered route', b=>b.routes.push(structuredClone(b.routes[0]))],
+    ['orphan rendered route', b=>b.routes.push({from:'i0p2',to:'i4p2'})],
+  ],
+  bonus: [
+    ['bonus above size', b=>b.islands[0].bonus=4],
+    ['incorrect entrance formula', b=>b.islands[0].bonus=2],
+  ],
+  fortress: [
+    ['large single entrance', b=>singleEntrance(b,'i6')],
+    ['four single-entrance islands', b=>{for(const id of ['i0','i1','i2','i3'])singleEntrance(b,id);}],
+  ],
+  concentration: [
+    ['single entrances exceed quarter of bonuses', b=>{for(const i of b.islands)singleEntrance(b,i.id);refreshBonuses(b);}],
+  ],
+  remoteness: [
+    ['five distinct island neighbours', b=>addSea(b,'i0p2','i4p2')],
+    ['more than four hops', b=>{for(const r of [...b.routes])removeSea(b,r.from,r.to);for(let i=0;i<8;i++)addSea(b,`i${i}p0`,`i${i+1}p0`);}],
+    ['unreachable island', b=>{for(const r of [...b.routes])if(r.from.startsWith('i8')||r.to.startsWith('i8'))removeSea(b,r.from,r.to);}],
+  ],
+  crowding: [
+    ['third sea crossing', b=>{addSea(b,'i0p0','i4p2');}],
+  ],
+};
+function singleEntrance(b, islandId) {
+  const ids=b.islands.find(i=>i.id===islandId).provinces;
+  const affected=b.routes.filter(r=>ids.includes(r.from)||ids.includes(r.to)).map(r=>({...r}));
+  for(const r of affected)removeSea(b,r.from,r.to);
+  for(const r of affected)addSea(b,ids[0],ids.includes(r.from)?r.to:r.from);
+}
+for (const [constraint, mutations] of Object.entries(cases)) {
+  test(`${constraint}: positive graph control`,()=>assert.deepEqual(checkConstraint(constraint,graphFixture()),[]));
+  for(const [name,mutate] of mutations)test(`${constraint}: rejects ${name}`,()=>{
+    const board=graphFixture();mutate(board);
+    assert.ok(checkConstraint(constraint,board).length>0,`${constraint} bypass: ${name}`);
+  });
+}

+# Seeded partial geography
+
+The construction uses our reviewed T64 geographical witness, not predecessor geometry. `witness-provenance.json` pins the source. `prepare-witness.mjs` strips all ownership, armies, production, sea adjacency and bonuses, normalizes common edge pieces and inserts the existing ports as vertices. The resulting data is a pure constant; generation reads no files or clock. All exported coordinates are integers in units of 1/2048 CSS px, exactly preserving the witness's dyadic port coordinates.
+
+`generateIslandGeography(seed, {attempts})` produces either an explicitly versioned partial geography or recoverable exhaustion. It never returns a playable `GameMap`. T35 consumes the entrance reservations to construct actual sea adjacency and bonuses; T36 owns new-game/UI integration and the 1,000-seed measure. Existing rules, default reference board, historical generation, saves and RNG streams are untouched.
+
+The seeded construction changes two eligible internal contacts through local T1 exchanges: an old pair loses a short shared edge and the opposite pair gains one. Four land-adjacency patterns result from these two choices. Land edges are independently re-derived from positive shared boundaries. Country/island IDs and sizes remain stable. This bounded constructive family does not sample arbitrary planar graphs or every possible island arrangement.
+
+Each island receives a seeded monotone piecewise-linear warp in both axes, placement jitter, and a shared whole-board reflection. All primitive shared edges are transformed canonically and split at warp knots, so opposite countries use identical boundary pieces. After placement, invalid or short reserved routes search alternative uniquely attached ports on the intended countries. Placement and port reservations pass or fail together; failed candidates are never relabelled as successes.
+
+## Limits and provenance
+
+| Value | Source |
+| --- | --- |
+| 46 countries; sizes 3,3,3,3,5,5,7,7,10; total degree 2–5 | Existing T24 approved parameters and T63 witness |
+| 50 attempts; at least99% seeds | T24 approved generation objective, unchanged |
+| Land degree at most4; at most2 corridor slots per country | Headroom for at least one sea edge under degree5; T24 crossing cap |
+| 40px hit squares, 44px square label gap | T24 approved display budget |
+| 44px horizontal / 47px vertical selected-name clearance | T64 retained native selected-label reservation |
+| Unique exposed ports; 8px competing-country margin; whole12px inward landing | T62 approved attachment contract |
+| No water/land contact; 10px unrelated-coast clearance; 20px span; 10px route separation | T62 approved water/traceability contract |
+| Fixed-point precision2048, quarter-pixel T1 half-edge, four warp intervals, at most0.5px expansion per interval and1px placement jitter, reflections | **[designed]** Construction choices measured in this task; not inferred predecessor rules |
+
+For those designed choices, the local search covered T24/T62/T63 and T64/T65 geometry studies. Reviewed upstream F022 leaves procedural construction unknown, as documented by T62. No predecessor asset, code or geometric table is used. The first broad-jitter draft and unrepaired77/100 sweep are retained; the algorithm was repaired without changing a constraint. Core coordinates and predicates use integer arithmetic. Warp cuts are exact BigInt rational fractions rounded once to the integer output grid; squared-distance comparisons use BigInt products. This avoids fractional intermediate coordinates and precision loss in large squared products. No game-rule probability/value is introduced.
+
+Failure records contain every rejected candidate and constraint class. The generator uses one continuous `DeterministicRng` stream per call, including retries, and returns its snapshot. Same seed and budget reproduce geometry, failure history and RNG exactly; each call returns fresh vectors. The zero-attempt path returns exhaustion without constructing a board.
+
+`acceptance.mjs` independently reconstructs a diagnostic scene from partial data and reservations, delegates to the unchanged T62/T24 checker and verifies partial-data boundaries, integer coordinates and headroom. Its temporary bonuses/sea lanes exist only in diagnostic data; the core API never exports them. Source omission controls and independent review rerun the actual implementation. Successful sweep data proves the measured family and seeds, not universal feasibility or owner appearance approval.

The sweep retains all100 outcomes, rejected candidates, constraint classes and replay hashes. They vary drawing on one graph and are distinct from the new four-topology construction. `evidence/flip-probe-Tg7Pmr` preserves accepted and failed local exchanges. +"""Archive large completed seed/source sets losslessly; retain loose originals."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import json,tarfile,hashlib
+root=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+sha=lambda b:hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest();count=0
+for out in (root/'evidence').iterdir():
+ if not out.is_dir()or not(out/'report.json').is_file()or(out/'measured-inputs-and-seeds.tar.gz').exists():continue
+ files=sorted([*out.glob('seed-*.json'),*out.glob('candidate-*.json'),*([p for p in (out/'sources').rglob('*')if p.is_file()]if(out/'sources').is_dir()else[])])

+ assert actual==hashes
+ (out/'archive-manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps({'sha256':sha((out/'measured-inputs-and-seeds.tar.gz').read_bytes()),'members':hashes,'originalLooseFilesPreserved':True},indent=2)+'\n')

+print('Completed archives:',count)

+"""Verify all recorded source/raw/member hashes, including disclosed supplements."""

+root=Path(__file__).resolve().parent;repo=root.parents[3];sha=lambda b:hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
+def members(p):
+ with tarfile.open(p)as t:return {m.name:sha(t.extractfile(m).read())for m in t if m.isfile()}
+checks=[]
+for p in sorted([*(root/'evidence').rglob('report.json'),*(root/'preflight').rglob('report.json')]):

+  observed={}

+  if not observed:

Index: docs/prototypes/new-game/T34/evidence/sweep-GvYjai/sources/docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/README.md
===================================================================
--- docs/prototypes/new-game/T34/evidence/sweep-GvYjai/sources/docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/README.md	
+++ docs/prototypes/new-game/T34/evidence/sweep-GvYjai/sources/docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/README.md	
@@ -0,0 +1,116 @@
+# T62: proposed country attachment and route contract for A
+
+This proposal replaces T24's facing-chain midpoint prescription **for dependent
+work only after the owner approves this contract**. It does not change T24,
+production, A's picture, graph or geometry. T60 A is the chosen visual direction;
+that choice does not approve these numeric limits. T63 must wait for a decision.
+
+The original malpaco [A fixture](../T60/evidence/build-LrdPTV/coast-first.json)
+and [baseline](../T60/evidence/build-LrdPTV/baseline.json) are pinned directly,
+without reading the mutable T60 study selector. The probe hashes both inputs,
+all checker dependencies, its source and acceptance tests. Reproduction writes a
+fresh directory and never repoints a selector or overwrites a measured report.
+
+## Proposed criteria
+
+All five new distances in [parameters.mjs](parameters.mjs) are **[designed]**.
+They are conservative choices compatible with this A reference, not inferred
+predecessor rules or established human recognition thresholds. Distances are CSS
+pixels at the existing 800×540 compact viewport with 800×460 usable board;
+the unchanged T24 scaling function applies to other coordinate frames.
+
+| Group | Proposed acceptance | Rationale and conflict |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Attachment | Each endpoint lies on the intended country's boundary **and** island silhouette, with no other country containing or touching it. | Retains exact exposed, unique attachment using T24's 1e-6 board-unit geometry tolerance. Internal borders, interior points and shared coast junctions reject. No new 1px snapping allowance. |
+| Attachment | At least **8px** from any competing country on the same island. | A's observed minimum is about 9.86px, baseline 27px. This reserves a measurable margin but explicitly accepts a smaller competitor margin than baseline. T60's 10px soft search preference was not a guarantee and would reject A. |
+| Attachment | Reverse the first/last route segment and continue **12px** into the intended country. The entire open continuation must stay strictly inside, including the final point. | Extends T60's 12px sample into a full segment check. Prevents a coast direction that suggests another country, and a notch exit/re-entry hidden by a final sample. Does not draw a landing mark or establish recognition. |
+| Water | Retain the complete T24 route/land intersection check. Additionally require **10px** from every unrelated island coastline along the whole polyline. | No land re-entry, boundary following or tangency is allowed, including source/destination. A's unrelated-coast minimum is about 64px; baseline about 1.5px. Endpoint islands are exempt only from the *extra* distance margin, never from no-land/no-touch checks. |
+| Traceability | Direct distance between route endpoints is at least **20px**. | A has three approximately 24px routes; a 25px threshold would reject it. Baseline has approximately 5.8px spans. Direct span prevents a long loop disguising a tiny water gap. No universal lower gap follows from archaeology. |
+| Traceability | Distance between every two route polylines is at least **10px**, including all endpoints and all shared-country pairs. | A's minimum is about 22px; baseline has six contacting pairs. No merge, crossing, shared port, endpoint crossing or near-parallel exception exists. Separate links of one country need separate ports. |
+| Traceability | No zero-length segment, positive adjacent reversal or nonadjacent self-contact. | Prevents self-merges and loops that cross themselves; forward collinear subdivision and ordinary noncrossing bends remain valid. |
+| Preserved | All **13** unaffected T24 categories run unchanged. | Counts, symmetry, connectivity, degree, cells, borders, crossings, bonus, fortress, concentration, remoteness, crowding and labels retain every existing rule and number. The legacy `intersections` category runs unchanged in `water`; only `coasts` is replaced by country attachment. |
+
+The proposed 20/10/8px distances deliberately leave some slack below the one
+chosen reference's observed minima; there is no optimization or perception
+experiment selecting them. The 12px continuation preserves the earlier explicit
+diagnostic distance. These values are separately reviewable owner decisions.
+Route length, detour ratio, bends and full legacy errors remain reported without
+inventing a maximum route length, bend budget or straight-only rule.
+
+## Evidence, sources and limits
+
+Run `node docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/probe.mjs`. Each retained report contains
+every criterion's description, individual values, evaluated/pass/fail counts,
+all four new group errors, all 15 legacy errors and the T60 route metrics for
+both boards. Read the fresh report path printed by the command. A must pass the
+proposal; the baseline is a comparison, not a required negative for each rule.
+
+The source rationale was checked against local reviewed archaeology F022 and
+the retained [T60 comparison and sources](../T60/README.md#sources-and-evidentiary-limits).
+[F022 at commit d5932c2](https://github.com/diegoami/isle-wars-archaeology/blob/d5932c2cea7741e81012bd4619e55430aba81a37/findings/F022-pro-map-presentation.md#answers)
+leaves midpoint placement, route construction and coast clearance unknown. Its
+three selected approximate visible spans are not whole-board bounds and support
+no universal gap or detour threshold. No predecessor files or geometry are
+imported. T24's original [designed parameters](../T24/parameters.mjs) remain the
+source for inherited graph, geometry, label, bonus and fairness constraints.
+T61's projection correction permits A's cells without waiving real slits/overlaps.
+
+The first retained [comparison](evidence/probe-eSYf7Z/summary.json) measured:
+
+| Criterion | Baseline failures / checks | A failures / checks |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| Unique exposed attachment | 0 / 30 | 0 / 30 |
+| 8px competing-country margin | 0 / 30 | 0 / 30 |
+| Whole 12px inward continuation | 2 / 30 | 0 / 30 |
+| Legacy route/land clearance | 0 / 15 | 0 / 15 |
+| 10px unrelated-coast margin | 1 / 15 | 0 / 15 |
+| 20px direct water span | 1 / 15 | 0 / 15 |
+| Self-tracing exclusions | 0 / 15 | 0 / 15 |
+| 10px separation of all route pairs | 6 / 105 | 0 / 105 |
+| Unaffected legacy categories | 0 / 13 | 0 / 13 |
+| Old midpoint prescription, disclosed conflict | 0 / 30 | 30 / 30 |
+
+The first report includes snapshots of its precise checker/probe sources;
+subsequent source/test/document changes have new fingerprints and fresh runs.
+
+There is one reference, not a generator or success-rate measurement. The existing
+99% within 50 attempts objective stays unproven; this proposal does not change it.
+Geometric attachment, distance and isolation are enforceable proxies. They cannot
+prove player comprehension, aesthetic quality or the feasibility of all future
+graphs. The owner retains visual judgment and may reject the thresholds, require
+stronger margins with a revised reference, or request a separate user study.
+
+## Verification and preservation
+
+Parent [contract.test.mjs](contract.test.mjs) remains byte-identical. Additional
+[guards](guards.test.mjs) isolate exact threshold edges, inward notches, hidden
+short gaps, shared-country separation, self-crossing/reversal and legacy
+delegation. Meaningful mutants for each inherited category compare the entire
+prefixed error list with the original checker, so connectivity errors cannot
+mask deletion of fortress or concentration. No assertion is weakened.
+
+The probe and validation scripts save fresh outputs, source hashes and original
+test logs inside this directory. Historical reports retain their source hashes;
+later source changes require a fresh report. Parent preflight files and all T24,
+T60 and T61 evidence stay untouched. Full-branch `git diff --check` must pass.
+
+`python3 docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/audit.py` deletes guards reversibly, runs
+both T62 suites, restores saved bytes in `finally`, and confirms every added test
+fails under at least one relevant deletion. It separately deletes all 13 legacy
+delegations, each new margin and each scaling factor. The retained mutant source
+edits and exact hashes permit reproduction without editing inherited files.
+Run this alone: it temporarily mutates T62's checker during its tests.
+
+`python3 docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/validate.py` runs the exact Done-when
+commands, both T62 suites, T24 and T61 regressions, both whitespace checks, and an
+empty-diff assertion for immutable parent/legacy paths. All terminal output is
+archived losslessly with exact per-member hashes, avoiding trailing-whitespace
+changes to originals. `report.json` records command tails and the fresh probe.
+
+The main-session audit found that the historical v2 index includes ignored loose
+preflight logs. Their exact bytes remain in `preflight/raw-logs.tar.gz`; they are
+not expected as loose files in a fresh clone. The current portable tracked-file
+index is `artifacts.v3.sha256.json`. Run `python3 docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/verify-evidence.py`
+to verify current files, report archive members, and all historical v2 loose-log
+hashes against their preserved archive bytes. Historical indexes/reports remain
+unchanged; source hashes identify the precise source used in each earlier run.

--- docs/prototypes/new-game/T34/evidence/sweep-GvYjai/sources/docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/audit.py	
+++ docs/prototypes/new-game/T34/evidence/sweep-GvYjai/sources/docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/audit.py	
@@ -0,0 +1,105 @@
+"""Retain reversible guard-deletion proof; never modify parent or legacy files."""
+import hashlib
+import io
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import subprocess
+import tarfile
+import tempfile
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+REPO = ROOT.parents[3]
+SOURCE = ROOT / 'contract.mjs'
+original = SOURCE.read_bytes()
+text = original.decode()
+out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='mutations-', dir=ROOT / 'evidence'))
+sha = lambda b: hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
+tests = ['docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/contract.test.mjs', 'docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/guards.test.mjs']
+command = ['node', '--test', '--test-reporter=tap', *tests]
+members = {}
+records = []
+mutants = []
+
+def add(name, old, new):
+    assert text.count(old) == 1, (name, text.count(old))
+    mutants.append((name, old, new))
+
+for group in ['attachment', 'water', 'traceability', 'preserved']:
+    anchor = "  if(group==='preserved')return preservedConstraints"
+    add('delete-group-' + group, anchor, f"  if(group==='{group}')return [];\n" + anchor)
+for category in ['counts','symmetry','connectivity','degree','cells','borders','crossings','bonus','fortress','concentration','remoteness','crowding','labels']:
+    add('delete-legacy-' + category, "!['coasts','intersections'].includes(n)", f"!['coasts','intersections','{category}'].includes(n)")
+for name, expression in [
+    ('competitor', 'margin<P.competingCountryMarginCss'),
+    ('unrelated-clearance', 'gap<P.unrelatedCoastClearanceCss'),
+    ('endpoint-span', 'distance(r.points[0],r.points.at(-1))*scale<P.endpointSpanCss'),
+    ('pair-separation', 'routeGap(x,y)*scale<P.routeSeparationCss'),
+    ('whole-inward', 'location(inward,p.polygon)!==1||segmentPieces(end,inward,p.polygon).pieces.some(p=>p.where!==1)'),
+    ('silhouette', '||location(end,island.polygon)!==0'),
+    ('ambiguous', 'board.provinces.some(q=>q.id!==id&&location(end,q.polygon)>=0)'),
+    ('zero-segment', 'distance(p,q)<=E'),
+    ('adjacent-reversal', 'onSegment(t,p,q)||onSegment(p,s,t)'),
+    ('self-contact', 'segmentGap(p,q,s,t)<=E'),
+]:
+    add('delete-' + name, expression, '' if name == 'silhouette' else 'false')
+add('sample-only-inward', '||segmentPieces(end,inward,p.polygon).pieces.some(p=>p.where!==1)', '')
+add('delete-legacy-water', "if(group==='water')errors.push(...legacy('intersections',board));", '')
+add('delete-segment-gap', 'export function segmentGap(a,b,c,d) {', 'export function segmentGap(a,b,c,d) { return Infinity;')
+for name, old, new in [
+    ('competitor', 'pointSegmentGap(end,a,b))))*scale', 'pointSegmentGap(end,a,b))))'),
+    ('inward', 'P.inwardContinuationCss/scale', 'P.inwardContinuationCss'),
+    ('unrelated-clearance', 'segmentGap(a,b,c,d))))*scale', 'segmentGap(a,b,c,d))))'),
+    ('endpoint-span', 'distance(r.points[0],r.points.at(-1))*scale', 'distance(r.points[0],r.points.at(-1))'),
+    ('pair-separation', 'routeGap(x,y)*scale', 'routeGap(x,y)'),
+]:
+    add('delete-scale-' + name, old, new)
+
+def run(name):
+    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, capture_output=True)
+    members[name + '.stdout.txt'] = result.stdout
+    members[name + '.stderr.txt'] = result.stderr
+    return result, re.findall(r'^not ok \d+ - (.+)$', result.stdout.decode(), re.M)
+
+try:
+    baseline, _ = run('before')
+    assert baseline.returncode == 0, 'Baseline must be green before mutation'
+    for name, old, new in mutants:
+        mutated = text.replace(old, new).encode()
+        SOURCE.write_bytes(mutated)
+        result, failed = run(name)
+        records.append({'name': name, 'replace': old, 'with': new, 'sourceSha256': sha(mutated), 'exit': result.returncode, 'failedTests': failed})
+        assert result.returncode == 1 and failed, 'Mutation survived or crashed outside tests: ' + name
+finally:
+    SOURCE.write_bytes(original)
+    assert SOURCE.read_bytes() == original
+    final, _ = run('restored')
+    members['contract.mjs.snapshot'] = original
+    failures = set().union(*(set(r['failedTests']) for r in records))
+    # Parent positives are expected to survive a deleted guard. Every additional
+    # test contains its own targeted negative, or directly checks segmentGap.
+    added = subprocess.run(['node','--test','--test-reporter=tap','docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/guards.test.mjs'], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True)
+    members['additional-restored.stdout.txt'] = added.stdout
+    members['additional-restored.stderr.txt'] = added.stderr
+    added_names = set(re.findall(r'^# Subtest: (.+)$', added.stdout.decode(), re.M))
+    with tarfile.open(out / 'raw-logs.tar.gz', 'w:gz') as archive:
+        for name, data in members.items():
+            entry = tarfile.TarInfo(name)
+            entry.size = len(data)
+            entry.mtime = 0
+            archive.addfile(entry, io.BytesIO(data))
+    # Validate exact archive bytes, including whitespace, before publishing hashes.
+    with tarfile.open(out / 'raw-logs.tar.gz') as archive:
+        assert all(archive.extractfile(name).read() == data for name, data in members.items())
+    report = {'command': command, 'sourceSha256': sha(original), 'restoredSha256': sha(SOURCE.read_bytes()),
+              'baselineExit': baseline.returncode, 'restoredExit': final.returncode, 'additionalRestoredExit': added.returncode,
+              'mutants': records, 'killed': sum(r['exit'] == 1 and bool(r['failedTests']) for r in records),
+              'additionalTests': len(added_names), 'additionalTestsNeverFailed': sorted(added_names - failures),
+              'fingerprints': {str(p.relative_to(REPO)): sha(p.read_bytes()) for p in [ROOT/'audit.py', ROOT/'guards.test.mjs', ROOT/'contract.test.mjs', ROOT/'parameters.mjs']},
+              'archiveSha256': sha((out/'raw-logs.tar.gz').read_bytes()), 'archiveMemberHashes': {name: sha(data) for name, data in members.items()}}
+    (out/'report.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2)+'\n')
+    print(json.dumps({'output': str(out.relative_to(REPO)), 'killed': report['killed'], 'mutants': len(mutants), 'restoredExit': final.returncode, 'additionalTestsNeverFailed': report['additionalTestsNeverFailed']}, indent=2))
+assert final.returncode == 0
+assert added.returncode == 0
+assert len(records) == len(mutants)
+assert not report['additionalTestsNeverFailed']

+"""Run the unchanged acceptance commands; retain exact logs in a fresh archive."""
+import hashlib
+import io
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import tarfile
+import tempfile
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+REPO = ROOT.parents[3]
+out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='acceptance-', dir=ROOT/'evidence'))
+sha = lambda b: hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
+prefix = 'docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/'
+commands = [['node', prefix+'probe.mjs']]
+commands += [['node','--test','--test-name-pattern='+group,prefix+'contract.test.mjs'] for group in ['attachment','water','traceability','preserved']]
+commands += [['git','diff','--check'], ['git','diff','--check','origin/main...HEAD'],
+             ['node','--test','--test-reporter=tap',prefix+'contract.test.mjs',prefix+'guards.test.mjs','docs/prototypes/new-game/T24/contract.test.mjs','docs/prototypes/new-game/T61/residual.test.mjs'],
+             ['git','diff','862bcf4','--','docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/contract.test.mjs','docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/preflight','docs/prototypes/new-game/T24','docs/prototypes/new-game/T60','docs/prototypes/new-game/T61']]
+members = {}
+records = []
+for number, command in enumerate(commands, 1):
+    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, capture_output=True)
+    for stream in ['stdout','stderr']:
+        members[f'{number:02d}.{stream}.txt'] = getattr(result, stream)
+    records.append({'command': command, 'exit': result.returncode, 'stdoutTail': result.stdout.decode().splitlines()[-12:], 'stderrTail': result.stderr.decode().splitlines()[-12:]})
+    print(json.dumps({'command': command, 'exit': result.returncode}), flush=True)
+probe_output = json.loads(members['01.stdout.txt'])['output']
+with tarfile.open(out/'raw-logs.tar.gz', 'w:gz') as archive:
+    for name, data in members.items():
+        entry = tarfile.TarInfo(name)
+        entry.size = len(data)
+        entry.mtime = 0
+        archive.addfile(entry, io.BytesIO(data))
+with tarfile.open(out/'raw-logs.tar.gz') as archive:
+    assert all(archive.extractfile(name).read() == data for name, data in members.items())
+paths = [p for p in ROOT.glob('*') if p.suffix in ['.mjs','.py','.md']]
+report = {'probeOutput': probe_output, 'commands': records,
+          'sourceHashes': {str(p.relative_to(REPO)): sha(p.read_bytes()) for p in paths},
+          'archiveSha256': sha((out/'raw-logs.tar.gz').read_bytes()), 'archiveMemberHashes': {name: sha(data) for name,data in members.items()},
+          'immutableParentAndLegacyDiffEmpty': members[f'{len(commands):02d}.stdout.txt'] == b''}
+(out/'report.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2)+'\n')
+print(json.dumps({'output': str(out.relative_to(REPO)), 'probeOutput': probe_output, 'allCommandsPass': all(r['exit'] == 0 for r in records), 'immutableParentAndLegacyDiffEmpty': report['immutableParentAndLegacyDiffEmpty']}, indent=2))
+assert all(r['exit'] == 0 for r in records)
+assert report['immutableParentAndLegacyDiffEmpty']

+"""Verify portable current artifacts and exact historical archived log bytes."""
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import tarfile
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+sha = lambda data: hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+index = json.loads((ROOT/'artifacts.v3.sha256.json').read_text())
+for name, expected in index['hashes'].items():
+    assert sha((ROOT/name).read_bytes()) == expected, name
+members = 0
+for report_path in (ROOT/'evidence').glob('*/report.json'):
+    report = json.loads(report_path.read_text())
+    if 'archiveMemberHashes' not in report:
+        continue
+    archive_path = report_path.parent/'raw-logs.tar.gz'
+    assert sha(archive_path.read_bytes()) == report['archiveSha256'], str(archive_path)
+    with tarfile.open(archive_path) as archive:
+        for name, expected in report['archiveMemberHashes'].items():
+            assert sha(archive.extractfile(name).read()) == expected, name
+            members += 1
+historical = json.loads((ROOT/'artifacts.v2.sha256.json').read_text())['hashes']

+            assert sha(archive.extractfile(name.removeprefix('preflight/')).read()) == expected, name

+print(f"Verified {len(index['hashes'])} tracked file hashes and {members} exact archived members")

+# Geographic feasibility contract
+
+T24 keeps the approved game constraints intact while measuring the existing implementation.
+The [first-iteration numerical contract](contract-proposal.md) was approved by the owner:
+40×40 CSS px hit areas, 44 px maximum-coordinate label separation, and an 800×460 board
+inside an 800×540 window. Coordinate, area and coast-centre tolerances are named in
+[parameters.mjs](parameters.mjs). The >=99% / <=50-candidate target is an objective to
+measure, not an assumption that the current generator achieves it.
+
+The approved rules are pinned in the proposal. In particular the canonical island-graph
+degree cap is **four**, even though production currently permits five. Country degree
+remains 2–5; crossings remain 14–18. No production files change here.
+
+## Run the acceptance
+
+Use Node 24 (22.15+ provides the TypeScript loader hooks, but this task was measured on 24):
+
+```sh
+node docs/prototypes/new-game/T24/probe.mjs
+node --test docs/prototypes/new-game/T24/contract.test.mjs
+node docs/prototypes/new-game/T24/mutations.mjs
+git diff --check
+```
+
+The task's 15 individual `--test-name-pattern` commands work as written. Tests began as
+parent-authored positive/mutated controls, committed before the checker. The retained
+mock transcripts show that a fixture mock passes while an accept-everything fake fails
+all negative cases. The real checker is then independently deletion-mutated one group
+at a time; each group must fail through assertions, then the saved bytes are restored
+in a `finally` and the complete suite reruns. Evidence records identical restoration hashes.
+
+Each probe/mutation run creates a fresh tracked-path evidence directory and prints its
+location. Earlier measurements are never overwritten. Default runs use all seeds 0–99
+and stop at the first accepted candidate or after 50 attempts. Per-seed files retain every
+candidate's map/scene hash, failure groups, observed attempt number and time, with detailed
+first-attempt failures. A continuous existing game RNG stream is used, advancing once
+after each rejected body just as the production retry boundary does. A source snapshot
+and a reproducibility hash distinguish semantic results from machine-dependent timings.
+
+`targetMet: false` is a valid measurement outcome; the CLI still exits zero if the
+measurement and its positive control ran correctly. It never silently reports a failed
+rate as success. A broken witness or runtime failure exits nonzero. Read the report's
+`targetMet`, not just the process exit status, before authorising downstream work.
+
+## What the checks establish
+
+[contract.mjs](contract.mjs) audits graph invariants and all five fairness checks.
+[geometry.mjs](geometry.mjs) checks finite simple polygons, containment/overlap, actual
+shared boundary lengths (including split/T-junction edges), exposed coasts, and route
+intersections. Point contacts are not borders. Coast chains comprise exposed directed
+edge pieces facing the destination island centre; contiguous pieces form chains. Choose
+the longest chain, with lexicographic start-point tie-break, then its arc-length midpoint.
+Every route endpoint must be on that country's exposed coast and within 1 CSS px of it.
+The route interior cannot touch or pass through land, including its source/destination.
+Sea routes may cross other sea routes: this probe does not certify visual lane separation.
+
+Label checks scale positions into the agreed compact board, require 40 px hit squares
+inside their countries and frame, and check 44 px maximum-coordinate spacing. The maximum
+coordinate distance avoids the mistake of using Euclidean separation alone for square
+hit areas. The 14 px text / 4.5:1 contrast fields express the schematic's specification;
+they are not measurements of a running browser. T52 must measure actual rendered text,
+palette, hit targets and ownership cues. No metadata can substitute for that UI acceptance.
+
+The [witness](witness.mjs) is a hand-arranged rectangular subdivision with 46 countries,
+nine islands and 16 crossings. Its geometry, ports and water paths are built independently
+of the checker, and it is inspected by the same checks as the baseline. This is **one
+schematic compatibility example**, not a new production generator, 100 different maps,
+visual approval, or a demonstrated generation success rate. Its SVG is a technical drawing.
+
+[existing.mjs](existing.mjs) reads production TypeScript without modifying it, applies the
+existing layout and coast function, and retains exact graph/polygon/label information.
+Its sea path diagnostics sample production's quadratic formula at 16 intervals; positive
+curved-path clearance is not certified. The centre endpoints are exact and already fail
+the coast requirement. Hit-size bounding-box estimates are upper bounds, and unmeasured
+contrast is marked unknown, never invented. The substantive border/gap/spacing failures
+do not depend on those unknown metadata fields or curve approximation.
+
+## Next gate
+
+The report must distinguish joint compatibility (a witness) from generator performance
+(the seed sweep). An existing implementation failing every trial does not prove the
+constraint set mathematically impossible. Preserve failures and the owner's constraints;
+obtain owner review of the resulting evidence before downstream algorithm work. The
+reference-board task also requires approval of exact topology and appearance. Do not
+promote this schematic as the intended Isle-Pro-like visual direction.
+
+## Measured result
+
+The authoritative [full-source-fingerprinted sweep](evidence/runs/run-bbMp5F/report.json)
+found **0/100 successful seeds after 5,000 candidates** (50 per seed). The witness passed
+all 15 groups. Every candidate failed cells, borders, coasts, intersections and labels;
+157 also failed remoteness/island degree. All other graph/fairness groups passed.
+
+The [schematic SVG](evidence/runs/run-bbMp5F/witness.svg) and
+[complete witness data](evidence/runs/run-bbMp5F/witness.json) show the positive control.
+[All acceptance pattern outputs](evidence/acceptance-v1/summary.json) pass, and
+[all 15 guard-deletion mutants](evidence/mutations/run-qjxt9M/report.json) were killed
+with byte-identical restoration and all 85 tests passing afterward.
+
+The earlier run-NKe9GQ sweep is retained as a preliminary measurement under the original
+checker (commit 9fd8f2f); it predates the explicit tiny-slit and finite-text regressions
+and full prototype-source fingerprinting. The authoritative rerun above includes those
+fixes. Both report zero existing-implementation successes; neither is proof that no
+future geographic generator can meet the target. The source-fingerprinted report is
+the result to use for decisions.
+
+The existing layout therefore needs geographic construction rather than more retries.
+Carry the current graph/fairness checks forward, but derive land links from actual
+shared subdivisions and choose sea endpoints from exposed coastline midpoints. Begin
+with an owner-approved reference board (T25) after owner review of this feasibility
+evidence. Keep the 99% / 50-attempt generation objective unproven until T34–T36 measure
+the replacement; this task does not authorise silent relaxation or production changes.
+
+## Review R1: protect scaled separation independently
+
+Kimi's round-1 review proved that deleting `*scale` from the spacing check left
+all 85 tests passing: the old resize control failed through hit-square containment
+instead of spacing. [The reproduced pre-fix result](evidence/rework-r1/before-tests.txt)
+is retained. The added control uses an enlarged frame giving scale 0.8: 50-unit
+cells still contain 40px hit squares exactly, but labels are only 40px apart, so
+only the 44px spacing check rejects them. It additionally asserts that every
+reported error is a spacing error, preventing the former confounding refusal.
+
+The [updated mutation audit](evidence/mutations/run-Po8FYb/report.json) kills all
+16 mutants: the 15 complete-group deletions and the targeted scale-only deletion.
+Source bytes restore exactly; all 86 tests then pass. The
+[updated task-pattern outputs](evidence/rework-r1/acceptance-v2/summary.json) also
+pass. The original 82/85-test and 15-mutant evidence remains historical evidence,
+not a claim about the extended suite. No production, checker or probe behaviour
+changed for R1, and every authoritative sweep source fingerprint still matches.
+Unknown contrast remains explicit; only a rendered UI check in T52 can establish it.

+# Geography contract for the feasibility probe
+
+The owner accepted these numerical values for the first iteration in the session
+following PR #105 (2026-10-15). The original proposal wording below is retained
+as design provenance. Acceptance does not establish the generation target.
+
+Sources: [canonical board rules](https://github.com/diegoami/isle-wars-archaeology/blob/ae298e37c2f5177039e55767607f9345b6cb0e7a/design/core-rules.md#the-board),
+[UI legibility](https://github.com/diegoami/isle-wars-archaeology/blob/ae298e37c2f5177039e55767607f9345b6cb0e7a/design/ui.md#legibility-and-size),
+and the owner's coast-centred crossing requirement. This is a proposed numerical
+contract for T24's probe, not permission to change a rule or a claim of generation success.
+
+## Constraints already decided
+
+| Check | Requirement |
+| --- | --- |
+| Counts | Exactly 46 distinct countries; nine distinct islands, sizes 3,3,3,3,5,5,7,7,10; each country in exactly one island, consistent with its island field |
+| Symmetry | Every land/sea edge exists in both directions; no missing endpoint, self edge, duplicate edge or wrong land/sea island classification |
+| Connectivity | The whole country graph, each island's land graph and the island graph are connected |
+| Degree | Every country has 2–5 distinct neighbours, including crossings |
+| Cells | Every country is a finite, positive-area, connected simple polygon; island silhouette is exactly its subdivision; interiors do not overlap; no unexplained gaps or overlaps between islands |
+| Borders | Land edges are exactly the within-island pairs sharing a positive-length boundary; a point contact does not create an edge |
+| Crossings | 14–18 undirected sea edges between islands; exactly one rendered route per edge |
+| Coasts | Route endpoints belong to the intended countries and lie at the arc-length midpoint of a maximal exposed coast chain facing the destination island; ties deterministic |
+| Intersections | The route interior avoids all country interiors, including re-entry into its own endpoint countries; routes may meet their intended coast only at their ends |
+| Bonus | Each island pays max(2, floor(size/2) + distinct entrance countries), never above size |
+| Fortress | No island of >=7 countries has one entrance; at most three islands have one entrance |
+| Concentration | Single-entrance island bonuses sum to at most one quarter of all bonuses |
+| Remoteness | Every island is at most four crossings from every other, and touches at most four other islands |
+| Crowding | No country carries more than two crossings |
+| Labels | Fit the approved minimum window with non-overlapping legible owner/count badges and hit areas; generator positions provide spacing |
+
+The pinned design's island-neighbour maximum is four. Production currently exports
+five in board-gen.ts/board-fairness.ts. This probe uses four, irrespective of that
+implementation difference. The parent smoke found no violations of four on seeds 0–99;
+this sample does not prove that production's looser guard cannot admit one elsewhere.
+
+## Numerical proposals for owner decision
+
+These are **[designed]** values: the canonical sources above and T23 inventory were
+searched; they fix the window but leave spacing/tolerances and generation budget open.
+
+| Property | Recommended value and meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| Minimum viewport | 800×540 CSS px, already approved in UI13 |
+| Probe's compact panel allowance | 80 CSS px total height, leaving an 800×460 board; an explicit allocation, not a measured final UI |
+| Country hit area | At least 40×40 CSS px; the approved design proposes 40 |
+| Label separation | At least 44 CSS px in the maximum-coordinate distance: 40 px badge/hit square plus 4 px gutter. This also guarantees at least 44 px Euclidean separation |
+| Count text | At least 14 CSS px, with >=4.5:1 contrast; both are the canonical UI proposals. Geometry alone cannot prove font/contrast rendering; T52 must measure the scene |
+| Reference frame | 800×460 for probe fixtures. Other frames scale to the same board area with aspect preserved; spacing is checked after scaling, never in unscaled source units |
+| Coordinate tolerance | 0.000001 reference unit for collinearity/point-on-edge comparisons; never a visual gap allowance |
+| Area tolerance | 0.0001 square reference units for accumulated subdivision-area arithmetic; explicit gap/overlap geometry is still checked |
+| Coast-centre tolerance | At most 1 CSS px from the computed chain midpoint; endpoints must still lie on the correct exposed coast |
+| Candidate generation budget | Target >=99% valid boards within at most 50 candidate attempts per seed, with explicit failure on exhaustion. This is a proposed downstream target, not a measured result or permission to retry a deterministic bad layout |
+
+The alternative spacing is 40 CSS px with no extra gutter. Keep 44 unless measurements
+show it prevents feasible subdivision; do not quietly shrink either the hit area or window.
+
+## What the first measurement establishes
+
+Run from this task's worktree with Node 24:
+
+```sh
+node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning docs/prototypes/new-game/T24/evidence/preflight/smoke.mjs
+```
+
+[baseline-v1.json](evidence/preflight/baseline-v1.json) retains every seed 0–99,
+one observed existing generator-body attempt per seed, map/scene hashes and timings.
+All 100 bodies returned boards. Minimum rendered label separation at the assumed
+800×460 board is 29.588 CSS px (Euclidean) / 28.884 CSS px (maximum-coordinate distance),
+below either spacing proposal. This is a failing baseline for label packing, not a proof
+that the proposed constraint set is impossible. It has not run the full geometry contract.
+
+T24 will distinguish a static jointly valid schematic witness, if one is found, from
+the seed sweep of the existing implementation. A witness proves compatibility of the
+constraints; it does not prove a generator meets its success rate, visual quality or variety.
+No synthetic fixture or relabelled copy may be reported as 100 distinct generated boards.
+The full probe must retain per-constraint failures and attempt counts, including failures;
+reruns write fresh evidence rather than overwrite measured outputs.
+
+Numerical contract approval is required by T24's label acceptance line and Hazards.
+Downstream algorithm work additionally requires the resulting feasibility evidence and
+owner approval; a failed existing baseline alone is no proof of joint infeasibility.

@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+# Seeded partial geography
+
+The construction uses our reviewed T64 geographical witness, not predecessor geometry. `witness-provenance.json` pins the source. `prepare-witness.mjs` strips all ownership, armies, production, sea adjacency and bonuses, normalizes common edge pieces and inserts the existing ports as vertices. The resulting data is a pure constant; generation reads no files or clock. All exported coordinates are integers in units of 1/2048 CSS px, exactly preserving the witness's dyadic port coordinates.
+
+`generateIslandGeography(seed, {attempts})` produces either an explicitly versioned partial geography or recoverable exhaustion. It never returns a playable `GameMap`. T35 consumes the entrance reservations to construct actual sea adjacency and bonuses; T36 owns new-game/UI integration and the 1,000-seed measure. Existing rules, default reference board, historical generation, saves and RNG streams are untouched.
+
+The seeded construction changes two eligible internal contacts through local T1 exchanges: an old pair loses a short shared edge and the opposite pair gains one. Four land-adjacency patterns result from these two choices. Land edges are independently re-derived from positive shared boundaries. Country/island IDs and sizes remain stable. This bounded constructive family does not sample arbitrary planar graphs or every possible island arrangement.
+
+Each island receives a seeded monotone piecewise-linear warp in both axes, placement jitter, and a shared whole-board reflection. All primitive shared edges are transformed canonically and split at warp knots, so opposite countries use identical boundary pieces. After placement, invalid or short reserved routes search alternative uniquely attached ports on the intended countries. Placement and port reservations pass or fail together; failed candidates are never relabelled as successes.
+
+## Limits and provenance
+
+| Value | Source |
+| --- | --- |
+| 46 countries; sizes 3,3,3,3,5,5,7,7,10; total degree 2–5 | Existing T24 approved parameters and T63 witness |
+| 50 attempts; at least99% seeds | T24 approved generation objective, unchanged |
+| Land degree at most4; at most2 corridor slots per country | Headroom for at least one sea edge under degree5; T24 crossing cap |
+| 40px hit squares, 44px square label gap | T24 approved display budget |
+| 44px horizontal / 47px vertical selected-name clearance | T64 retained native selected-label reservation |
+| Unique exposed ports; 8px competing-country margin; whole12px inward landing | T62 approved attachment contract |
+| No water/land contact; 10px unrelated-coast clearance; 20px span; 10px route separation | T62 approved water/traceability contract |
+| Fixed-point precision2048, quarter-pixel T1 half-edge, four warp intervals, at most0.5px expansion per interval and1px placement jitter, reflections | **[designed]** Construction choices measured in this task; not inferred predecessor rules |
+
+For those designed choices, the local search covered T24/T62/T63 and T64/T65 geometry studies. Reviewed upstream F022 leaves procedural construction unknown, as documented by T62. No predecessor asset, code or geometric table is used. The first broad-jitter draft and unrepaired77/100 sweep are retained; the algorithm was repaired without changing a constraint. Core coordinates and predicates use integer arithmetic. Warp cuts are exact BigInt rational fractions rounded once to the integer output grid; squared-distance comparisons use BigInt products. This avoids fractional intermediate coordinates and precision loss in large squared products. No game-rule probability/value is introduced.
+
+Failure records contain every rejected candidate and constraint class. The generator uses one continuous `DeterministicRng` stream per call, including retries, and returns its snapshot. Same seed and budget reproduce geometry, failure history and RNG exactly; each call returns fresh vectors. The zero-attempt path returns exhaustion without constructing a board.
+

Index: docs/prototypes/new-game/T34/evidence/sweep-auuZI2/sources/docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/README.md
===================================================================
--- docs/prototypes/new-game/T34/evidence/sweep-auuZI2/sources/docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/README.md	
+++ docs/prototypes/new-game/T34/evidence/sweep-auuZI2/sources/docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/README.md	
@@ -0,0 +1,116 @@
+# T62: proposed country attachment and route contract for A
+
+This proposal replaces T24's facing-chain midpoint prescription **for dependent
+work only after the owner approves this contract**. It does not change T24,
+production, A's picture, graph or geometry. T60 A is the chosen visual direction;
+that choice does not approve these numeric limits. T63 must wait for a decision.
+
+The original malpaco [A fixture](../T60/evidence/build-LrdPTV/coast-first.json)
+and [baseline](../T60/evidence/build-LrdPTV/baseline.json) are pinned directly,
+without reading the mutable T60 study selector. The probe hashes both inputs,
+all checker dependencies, its source and acceptance tests. Reproduction writes a
+fresh directory and never repoints a selector or overwrites a measured report.
+
+## Proposed criteria
+
+All five new distances in [parameters.mjs](parameters.mjs) are **[designed]**.
+They are conservative choices compatible with this A reference, not inferred
+predecessor rules or established human recognition thresholds. Distances are CSS
+pixels at the existing 800×540 compact viewport with 800×460 usable board;
+the unchanged T24 scaling function applies to other coordinate frames.
+
+| Group | Proposed acceptance | Rationale and conflict |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Attachment | Each endpoint lies on the intended country's boundary **and** island silhouette, with no other country containing or touching it. | Retains exact exposed, unique attachment using T24's 1e-6 board-unit geometry tolerance. Internal borders, interior points and shared coast junctions reject. No new 1px snapping allowance. |
+| Attachment | At least **8px** from any competing country on the same island. | A's observed minimum is about 9.86px, baseline 27px. This reserves a measurable margin but explicitly accepts a smaller competitor margin than baseline. T60's 10px soft search preference was not a guarantee and would reject A. |
+| Attachment | Reverse the first/last route segment and continue **12px** into the intended country. The entire open continuation must stay strictly inside, including the final point. | Extends T60's 12px sample into a full segment check. Prevents a coast direction that suggests another country, and a notch exit/re-entry hidden by a final sample. Does not draw a landing mark or establish recognition. |
+| Water | Retain the complete T24 route/land intersection check. Additionally require **10px** from every unrelated island coastline along the whole polyline. | No land re-entry, boundary following or tangency is allowed, including source/destination. A's unrelated-coast minimum is about 64px; baseline about 1.5px. Endpoint islands are exempt only from the *extra* distance margin, never from no-land/no-touch checks. |
+| Traceability | Direct distance between route endpoints is at least **20px**. | A has three approximately 24px routes; a 25px threshold would reject it. Baseline has approximately 5.8px spans. Direct span prevents a long loop disguising a tiny water gap. No universal lower gap follows from archaeology. |
+| Traceability | Distance between every two route polylines is at least **10px**, including all endpoints and all shared-country pairs. | A's minimum is about 22px; baseline has six contacting pairs. No merge, crossing, shared port, endpoint crossing or near-parallel exception exists. Separate links of one country need separate ports. |
+| Traceability | No zero-length segment, positive adjacent reversal or nonadjacent self-contact. | Prevents self-merges and loops that cross themselves; forward collinear subdivision and ordinary noncrossing bends remain valid. |
+| Preserved | All **13** unaffected T24 categories run unchanged. | Counts, symmetry, connectivity, degree, cells, borders, crossings, bonus, fortress, concentration, remoteness, crowding and labels retain every existing rule and number. The legacy `intersections` category runs unchanged in `water`; only `coasts` is replaced by country attachment. |
+
+The proposed 20/10/8px distances deliberately leave some slack below the one
+chosen reference's observed minima; there is no optimization or perception
+experiment selecting them. The 12px continuation preserves the earlier explicit
+diagnostic distance. These values are separately reviewable owner decisions.
+Route length, detour ratio, bends and full legacy errors remain reported without
+inventing a maximum route length, bend budget or straight-only rule.
+
+## Evidence, sources and limits
+
+Run `node docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/probe.mjs`. Each retained report contains
+every criterion's description, individual values, evaluated/pass/fail counts,
+all four new group errors, all 15 legacy errors and the T60 route metrics for
+both boards. Read the fresh report path printed by the command. A must pass the
+proposal; the baseline is a comparison, not a required negative for each rule.
+
+The source rationale was checked against local reviewed archaeology F022 and
+the retained [T60 comparison and sources](../T60/README.md#sources-and-evidentiary-limits).
+[F022 at commit d5932c2](https://github.com/diegoami/isle-wars-archaeology/blob/d5932c2cea7741e81012bd4619e55430aba81a37/findings/F022-pro-map-presentation.md#answers)
+leaves midpoint placement, route construction and coast clearance unknown. Its
+three selected approximate visible spans are not whole-board bounds and support
+no universal gap or detour threshold. No predecessor files or geometry are
+imported. T24's original [designed parameters](../T24/parameters.mjs) remain the
+source for inherited graph, geometry, label, bonus and fairness constraints.
+T61's projection correction permits A's cells without waiving real slits/overlaps.
+
+The first retained [comparison](evidence/probe-eSYf7Z/summary.json) measured:
+
+| Criterion | Baseline failures / checks | A failures / checks |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| Unique exposed attachment | 0 / 30 | 0 / 30 |
+| 8px competing-country margin | 0 / 30 | 0 / 30 |
+| Whole 12px inward continuation | 2 / 30 | 0 / 30 |
+| Legacy route/land clearance | 0 / 15 | 0 / 15 |
+| 10px unrelated-coast margin | 1 / 15 | 0 / 15 |
+| 20px direct water span | 1 / 15 | 0 / 15 |
+| Self-tracing exclusions | 0 / 15 | 0 / 15 |
+| 10px separation of all route pairs | 6 / 105 | 0 / 105 |
+| Unaffected legacy categories | 0 / 13 | 0 / 13 |
+| Old midpoint prescription, disclosed conflict | 0 / 30 | 30 / 30 |
+
+The first report includes snapshots of its precise checker/probe sources;
+subsequent source/test/document changes have new fingerprints and fresh runs.
+
+There is one reference, not a generator or success-rate measurement. The existing
+99% within 50 attempts objective stays unproven; this proposal does not change it.
+Geometric attachment, distance and isolation are enforceable proxies. They cannot
+prove player comprehension, aesthetic quality or the feasibility of all future
+graphs. The owner retains visual judgment and may reject the thresholds, require
+stronger margins with a revised reference, or request a separate user study.
+
+## Verification and preservation
+
+Parent [contract.test.mjs](contract.test.mjs) remains byte-identical. Additional
+[guards](guards.test.mjs) isolate exact threshold edges, inward notches, hidden
+short gaps, shared-country separation, self-crossing/reversal and legacy
+delegation. Meaningful mutants for each inherited category compare the entire
+prefixed error list with the original checker, so connectivity errors cannot
+mask deletion of fortress or concentration. No assertion is weakened.
+
+The probe and validation scripts save fresh outputs, source hashes and original
+test logs inside this directory. Historical reports retain their source hashes;
+later source changes require a fresh report. Parent preflight files and all T24,
+T60 and T61 evidence stay untouched. Full-branch `git diff --check` must pass.
+
+`python3 docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/audit.py` deletes guards reversibly, runs
+both T62 suites, restores saved bytes in `finally`, and confirms every added test
+fails under at least one relevant deletion. It separately deletes all 13 legacy
+delegations, each new margin and each scaling factor. The retained mutant source
+edits and exact hashes permit reproduction without editing inherited files.
+Run this alone: it temporarily mutates T62's checker during its tests.
+
+`python3 docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/validate.py` runs the exact Done-when
+commands, both T62 suites, T24 and T61 regressions, both whitespace checks, and an
+empty-diff assertion for immutable parent/legacy paths. All terminal output is
+archived losslessly with exact per-member hashes, avoiding trailing-whitespace
+changes to originals. `report.json` records command tails and the fresh probe.
+
+The main-session audit found that the historical v2 index includes ignored loose
+preflight logs. Their exact bytes remain in `preflight/raw-logs.tar.gz`; they are
+not expected as loose files in a fresh clone. The current portable tracked-file
+index is `artifacts.v3.sha256.json`. Run `python3 docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/verify-evidence.py`
+to verify current files, report archive members, and all historical v2 loose-log
+hashes against their preserved archive bytes. Historical indexes/reports remain
+unchanged; source hashes identify the precise source used in each earlier run.

--- docs/prototypes/new-game/T34/evidence/sweep-auuZI2/sources/docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/audit.py	
+++ docs/prototypes/new-game/T34/evidence/sweep-auuZI2/sources/docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/audit.py	
@@ -0,0 +1,105 @@
+"""Retain reversible guard-deletion proof; never modify parent or legacy files."""
+import hashlib
+import io
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import subprocess
+import tarfile
+import tempfile
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+REPO = ROOT.parents[3]
+SOURCE = ROOT / 'contract.mjs'
+original = SOURCE.read_bytes()
+text = original.decode()
+out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='mutations-', dir=ROOT / 'evidence'))
+sha = lambda b: hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
+tests = ['docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/contract.test.mjs', 'docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/guards.test.mjs']
+command = ['node', '--test', '--test-reporter=tap', *tests]
+members = {}
+records = []
+mutants = []
+
+def add(name, old, new):
+    assert text.count(old) == 1, (name, text.count(old))
+    mutants.append((name, old, new))
+
+for group in ['attachment', 'water', 'traceability', 'preserved']:
+    anchor = "  if(group==='preserved')return preservedConstraints"
+    add('delete-group-' + group, anchor, f"  if(group==='{group}')return [];\n" + anchor)
+for category in ['counts','symmetry','connectivity','degree','cells','borders','crossings','bonus','fortress','concentration','remoteness','crowding','labels']:
+    add('delete-legacy-' + category, "!['coasts','intersections'].includes(n)", f"!['coasts','intersections','{category}'].includes(n)")
+for name, expression in [
+    ('competitor', 'margin<P.competingCountryMarginCss'),
+    ('unrelated-clearance', 'gap<P.unrelatedCoastClearanceCss'),
+    ('endpoint-span', 'distance(r.points[0],r.points.at(-1))*scale<P.endpointSpanCss'),
+    ('pair-separation', 'routeGap(x,y)*scale<P.routeSeparationCss'),
+    ('whole-inward', 'location(inward,p.polygon)!==1||segmentPieces(end,inward,p.polygon).pieces.some(p=>p.where!==1)'),
+    ('silhouette', '||location(end,island.polygon)!==0'),
+    ('ambiguous', 'board.provinces.some(q=>q.id!==id&&location(end,q.polygon)>=0)'),
+    ('zero-segment', 'distance(p,q)<=E'),
+    ('adjacent-reversal', 'onSegment(t,p,q)||onSegment(p,s,t)'),
+    ('self-contact', 'segmentGap(p,q,s,t)<=E'),
+]:
+    add('delete-' + name, expression, '' if name == 'silhouette' else 'false')
+add('sample-only-inward', '||segmentPieces(end,inward,p.polygon).pieces.some(p=>p.where!==1)', '')
+add('delete-legacy-water', "if(group==='water')errors.push(...legacy('intersections',board));", '')
+add('delete-segment-gap', 'export function segmentGap(a,b,c,d) {', 'export function segmentGap(a,b,c,d) { return Infinity;')
+for name, old, new in [
+    ('competitor', 'pointSegmentGap(end,a,b))))*scale', 'pointSegmentGap(end,a,b))))'),
+    ('inward', 'P.inwardContinuationCss/scale', 'P.inwardContinuationCss'),
+    ('unrelated-clearance', 'segmentGap(a,b,c,d))))*scale', 'segmentGap(a,b,c,d))))'),
+    ('endpoint-span', 'distance(r.points[0],r.points.at(-1))*scale', 'distance(r.points[0],r.points.at(-1))'),
+    ('pair-separation', 'routeGap(x,y)*scale', 'routeGap(x,y)'),
+]:
+    add('delete-scale-' + name, old, new)
+
+def run(name):
+    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=REPO, capture_output=True)
+    members[name + '.stdout.txt'] = result.stdout
+    members[name + '.stderr.txt'] = result.stderr
+    return result, re.findall(r'^not ok \d+ - (.+)$', result.stdout.decode(), re.M)
+
+try:
+    baseline, _ = run('before')
+    assert baseline.returncode == 0, 'Baseline must be green before mutation'
+    for name, old, new in mutants:
+        mutated = text.replace(old, new).encode()
+        SOURCE.write_bytes(mutated)
+        result, failed = run(name)
+        records.append({'name': name, 'replace': old, 'with': new, 'sourceSha256': sha(mutated), 'exit': result.returncode, 'failedTests': failed})
+        assert result.returncode == 1 and failed, 'Mutation survived or crashed outside tests: ' + name
+finally:
+    SOURCE.write_bytes(original)
+    assert SOURCE.read_bytes() == original
+    final, _ = run('restored')
+    members['contract.mjs.snapshot'] = original
+    failures = set().union(*(set(r['failedTests']) for r in records))
+    # Parent positives are expected to survive a deleted guard. Every additional
+    # test contains its own targeted negative, or directly checks segmentGap.
+    added = subprocess.run(['node','--test','--test-reporter=tap','docs/prototypes/new-game/T62/guards.test.mjs'], cwd=REPO, capture_output=True)
+    members['additional-restored.stdout.txt'] = added.stdout
+    members['additional-restored.stderr.txt'] = added.stderr
+    added_names = set(re.findall(r'^# Subtest: (.+)$', added.stdout.decode(), re.M))
+    with tarfile.open(out / 'raw-logs.tar.gz', 'w:gz') as archive:
+        for name, data in members.items():
+            entry = tarfile.TarInfo(name)
+            entry.size = len(data)
+            entry.mtime = 0
+            archive.addfile(entry, io.BytesIO(data))
+    # Validate exact archive bytes, including whitespace, before publishing hashes.
+    with tarfile.open(out / 'raw-logs.tar.gz') as archive:
+        assert all(archive.extractfile(name).read() == data for name, data in members.items())
+    report = {'command': command, 'sourceSha256': sha(original), 'restoredSha256': sha(SOURCE.read_bytes()),
+              'baselineExit': baseline.returncode, 'restoredExit': final.returncode, 'additionalRestoredExit': added.returncode,
+              'mutants': records, 'killed': sum(r['exit'] == 1 and bool(r['failedTests']) for r in records),
+              'additionalTests': len(added_names), 'additionalTestsNeverFailed': sorted(added_names - failures),
+              'fingerprints': {str(p.relative_to(REPO)): sha(p.read_bytes()) for p in [ROOT/'audit.py', ROOT/'guards.test.mjs', ROOT/'contract.test.mjs', ROOT/'parameters.mjs']},

+"""Render exact acceptance tails without routing Markdown through a shell."""

+body = (root/'pr-body.md').read_text()
+start = body.index('Done-when commands and actual output tails')
